salesVolume.title: Electric sales volume
salesVolume.content:
Sales volume is total electric GWh delivered across Evergy's Kansas Central and Metro (Missouri) franchises.

For Evergy, Inc.: volume growth is the tell for whether the signed large-load (data-center) pipeline is actually energizing -- 2.6-3.1 GW is signed today against a 5-7 GW target, and Evergy earns its allowed ROE (9.4-9.7%) on the rate base built to serve that load whether or not usage shows up immediately. Revenue and earnings are driven primarily by the regulated capex plan and rate cases, not by volume alone.

What to watch:

  • A step-up in GWh as signed large-load agreements begin energizing
  • Weather-driven swings in residential/commercial volume versus the structural large-load trend

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Evergy, Inc.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Evergy, Inc.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Evergy, Inc.: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Evergy, Inc.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure.

For Evergy, Inc.: reported FCF has been negative every year since FY2021 (FY2025: -$751.7m; 9M-2026: -$1,015m) because the $21.6B 2026-2030 capital plan runs well ahead of operating cash flow. That capex earns a regulated 9.4-9.7% allowed ROE once admitted to rate base, so this is the capex-supercycle signature of a regulated utility funding rate-base growth, not distress -- it is why the DCF values Evergy as a dividend discount at cost of equity rather than an owner-FCF model (an unlevered FCF DCF would value the equity near nothing, a method artefact).

What to watch:

  • OCF growth relative to the capex plan -- a shrinking OCF share of funding signals rising reliance on debt/equity issuance
  • Equity issuance (ATM/forward programme) diluting EPS growth versus rate-base growth

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Evergy, Inc.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Evergy, Inc.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Evergy, Inc.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line across Evergy's Kansas Central and Metro (Missouri) regulated electric franchises.

For Evergy, Inc.: revenue includes a fuel/purchased-power pass-through that earns no return, so it is a noisier signal than rate base or allowed ROE -- the DCF discounts dividends (adjusted EPS x payout), not this line. Watch rate-case outcomes and large-load energization rather than revenue growth alone.

What to watch:

  • Rate-case decisions in Kansas and Missouri moving the allowed revenue requirement
  • Large-load/data-center energization (2.6-3.1 GW signed vs. a 5-7 GW target) lifting volume-driven revenue
  • Interim rows show seasonality (summer cooling, winter heating)

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Evergy, Inc.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
